ONGC takes over disputed Cambay block from Vedanta after court ruling
items.summary:
State-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) has taken over operations and control of the disputed Cambay offshore block from Vedanta Oil & Gas Ltd following a Delhi High Court ruling, according to regulatory filings by the two companies.
Vedanta Oil & Gas Ltd has recognised an impairment charge of about Rs 379 crore against assets and receivables linked to the block.
The takeover of the CB-OS-02 block took effect on July 22, 2026, after the High Court's single-judge bench dismissed Vedanta's challenge to the government's decision not to extend the production-sharing contract, ONGC said in its quarterly filing.
The block was operated by Vedanta, which held a 40 per cent participating interest; ONGC held 50 per cent, and Invenire Petrodyne Ltd had the remaining 10 per cent.
The government, through a September 19, 2025, letter, declined to extend the contract and directed the operator to hand over the block to ONGC.
Vedanta challenged the decision before the Delhi High Court

items.summary:
Edelweiss Financial Services on Friday reported an 18 per cent growth in consolidated net profit to Rs 207 crore for the second quarter ended September.
The company had earned a profit of Rs 175 crore in the corresponding quarter of the preceding fiscal.
Total income increased to Rs 2,602 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared to Rs 1,900 crore in the year-ago period, Edelweiss Financial Services said in a regulatory filing.
Interest income rose to Rs 720 crore from Rs 687 crore in the same quarter a year ago.
During the quarter, total expenses also rose to Rs 2,393 crore from Rs 1,946 crore in the same period a year ago.
The company completed the Rs 1,200-crore IPO of its subsidiary Edelweiss Alternatives last month.
Earlier this year, global investment management firm Carlyle became a strategic majority investor in another subsidiary of the company, Nido Home Finance, with an investment of Rs 2,000 crore.
